headline: Majors hold 200-day support with overbought momentum; whales moving BTC onto exchanges while stablecoins flat and leverage crowded across altcoins.
paragraphs: The regime is unified: all seven majors sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and six of seven have completed golden crosses (XRP and DOGE are above the 200-day but lack the cross). Bitcoin and Ethereum lead with the cleanest setups, both crossing above 200-day lines and showing trend alignment. On the month, Bitcoin is up 25.2%, Ethereum up 37.5%, and the broader cohort has rallied hard: SOL up 50.3% on the month, XRP up 38.6%, ADA up 13.5%. The crowd is pricing growth; the tape reflects it.

Momentum, however, reads overbought across the board without conviction underneath. Bitcoin RSI sits at 64.2 and Ethereum at 65.4, both elevated but not yet extreme. What matters: Bitcoin and Ethereum both show MACD below signal line despite the price rise, a classic divergence between momentum and trend. SOL and ADA are the only two with MACD above signal, so they hold positive momentum structure. The day's tape reflects caution: Bitcoin up just 0.4%, Ethereum up 0.7%, SOL down 1.8% on the day. The month-long rally is breathing, not accelerating. Volatility has expanded: Bitcoin 30-day realized vol at 44.1%, Ethereum at 52.6%, XRP at 84.2%, ADA at 88.5%. Wide range, thin conviction.

Derivatives positioning reveals crowding and expense in the bet. Bitcoin funding rates stand at 0.96% per eight hours, annualized to 10.5%, well above comfort for a market that has already rallied 25% in a month. Ethereum and SOL are equally rich at 5.1% and 11% annualized, respectively. More telling: Bitcoin's long/short ratio is 1.04 (longs only modestly ahead), but SOL has swung to 1.82, DOGE to 3.66, and XRP to 2.05. The altcoin complex has become overwhelmingly long. In the last two hours for Bitcoin, 100 liquidations fired: 1.07 million dollars of longs, only 30,000 of shorts. Ethereum reversed that sharply, with 1.07 million shorts liquidated versus 443,000 longs, suggesting the long bias in Ethereum futures may be a weak hand. Open interest remains substantial (Bitcoin 2.45 billion, Ethereum 1.53 billion), keeping the float in play.

Flow signals display a tension worth watching. Over the last two days, Bitcoin moved 81.1 million dollars onto exchanges (Binance specifically), a concrete supply addition at the margin. ETH ETF flows disagreed: on 18 Sep the spot ETF saw 143.7 million inflow, but over the prior five sessions the net was negative 140.6 million, marking a single-day spike after four days of outflow. BTC spot ETFs showed stability, with 433 million inflow on 18 Sep and a five-session net of positive 6.1 million. The stablecoin float sits at 310 billion, up only 0.68% on the month, well below the rally magnitude. Whales moving Bitcoin onto exchanges while stablecoin dry powder sits flat suggests sellers are arriving at the margin, not buyers repositioning.

Whale flows over the last 48 hours showed 81.1 million Bitcoin moving onto exchanges, paired with 255 million dollars in stablecoins (USDT 150 million, USDC 105 million) moving off exchanges from Binance. This is the classic pattern of profit-taking: coins flowing in to be sold, stables flowing out because they are already deployed. The weekly trend deepens the read: week ending Sep 13 saw 827 million onto exchanges, week ending Sep 20 saw 653 million more, reversing the one outflow week (Sep 6, 494 million off) in early September. That is three weeks of cumulative selling pressure from big accounts.

Sentiment remains in Greed at 71, near the top of the 30-day range (50 to 74), but the tape underneath is hesitant. Market cap fell 2.57% on the day despite modest green on the majors, suggesting breadth is breaking. Bitcoin dominance at 58.7% is stable. The specific condition to watch: if Bitcoin MACD recrosses above signal while funding remains above 10% annualized and whales continue onto exchanges, that divergence (momentum accelerating while supply is being added at the margin) would be the first genuine warning sign. Equally, if stablecoin float drops sharply or reverses the low-velocity trend, that would signal demand is reloading.
